title: Why Small Heat Pumps Beat Large Ones on SCOP
author: Heat Pump Database
summary: Our data shows residential ASHPs between 4-20kW post noticeably higher SCOP than commercial units above 20kW - even when refrigerant and test conditions are matched. Here's what's actually driving the gap.
body_html:
Anyone who spends time in the Visualise section of this database will have noticed the same thing: plot SCOP against maximum heating capacity, and there's a visible step down once you cross roughly 20kW. Products in the 4–20kW band, which covers most UK homes, cluster noticeably higher than the commercial-scale units above it. We dug into the underlying data to find out whether that's a real effect or an artefact of how the chart is drawn, and if real, why it happens.

The pattern holds up under scrutiny

The naive comparison (every product with a published SCOP, split at 20kW) shows a modest gap: 4.79 average SCOP for 4–20kW products versus 4.64 for those above 20kW. That's real but small, and it's diluted by mixing heat pump types: ground and water source units, which behave differently from air source, are unevenly distributed between the two bands.

Once we control for that, looking only at air source heat pumps tested at the same flow-temperature condition (SCOP at W35, the standard EN 14825 basis), the gap widens substantially: 4.68 average SCOP for 4–20kW ASHPs, versus 3.92 for those above 20kW. That's a 15–20% relative difference, and it holds within every major refrigerant type we checked:

Refrigerant4-20kW mean SCOP>20kW mean SCOP
R324.694.03
R2904.874.16
R410A4.213.69

So it isn't simply that small heat pumps happen to use a more efficient refrigerant blend. Something else is going on.

It's really a residential-vs-commercial split

The clearest signal in the data is who's making these products. In the 4–20kW band, 94% of listings are residential units, dominated by brands like Daikin, Panasonic, LG, Riello and Baxi. Above 20kW, 98% are commercial units, dominated by HVAC specialists like Rhoss, Swegon, Clivet, Carrier and Trane. These are almost entirely disjoint markets, and that matters more than the capacity number itself.

Residential ASHPs compete on SCOP because it's tied directly to UK policy: MCS listing, SAP calculations and Boiler Upgrade Scheme eligibility all hinge on the published figure. Commercial equipment isn't sold against the same yardstick, so there's less commercial pressure to optimise for it.

Modulation, not just marketing

Most small residential ASHPs use a single variable-speed inverter compressor that can turn down to a small fraction of its rated output. SCOP is a seasonal average dominated by part-load conditions, mild autumn and spring days rather than the coldest day of the year, so a compressor that modulates smoothly down low is exactly what the metric rewards.

Larger commercial systems more often reach their capacity by staging multiple compressors on and off rather than continuously modulating one, which is a sensible way to guarantee output for a building but tends to be less efficient at partial load, precisely the condition SCOP weights most heavily.

Two explanations we ruled out

Before settling on the above, we checked two obvious alternatives:

Are the big units just working harder, with higher flow temperatures? No. If anything, the 4–20kW band has a slightly higher average maximum flow temperature (67°C vs 60°C), which should hurt their SCOP relative to the larger units, not help it.

Is this just a reporting gap: do fewer large commercial products even publish SCOP? Partly, but not enough to explain it. 73% of 4–20kW products in the database list an SCOP figure, versus 63% of those above 20kW: a real gap consistent with SCOP being a residential/policy-driven metric, but far too small on its own to account for a 0.7-point difference in the average.

The takeaway

If you're comparing a domestic-scale heat pump against something plumbed for a larger building, don't expect the SCOP figures to be comparable on the same terms: they're drawn from different markets with different design priorities and different regulatory pressure. For sizing a home, the 4–20kW figures in this database remain the fair like-for-like comparison; for commercial specification, capacity, reliability and total installed cost typically matter more than chasing the last point of seasonal efficiency.

Sources & further reading

The mechanisms behind this gap (part-load behaviour, compressor modulation and the different regulatory pressure on residential versus commercial equipment) are corroborated by independent industry and technical sources:

  • Lochinvar – “SCOP vs COP: What Engineers, Specifiers, and M&E Contractors Need to Know for Commercial Decarbonisation Projects”, on why SCOP carries different weight and regulatory drivers in commercial specification than in the residential market.
  • IDM Energie – “Part-Load Operation in Heat Pumps”, explaining why modulating systems achieve higher seasonal efficiency because COP improves at part load, and buildings spend most of their time there.
  • IDM Energie – “EN 14825 Standard: Heat Pump Seasonal Performance Testing”, on how the standard this database’s SCOP figures are drawn from explicitly weights part-load performance rather than a single full-load point.
  • HVAC Know It All – “Variable Speed Scroll Compressors: Why They Dominate Modern Heat Pumps”, on why continuously modulating compressors outperform staged/cycling designs at part load, the operating pattern more common in larger commercial units.
image_credit: Heat Pump Database, SCOP vs. maximum heating capacity across all listed products
tldr: Small heat pumps (4–20kW) post meaningfully higher SCOP than large commercial units, mainly because residential kit is optimised for SCOP and uses modulating compressors, while commercial systems stage multiple compressors and aren't benchmarked the same way.
seo_title: Why Small Heat Pumps Beat Large Ones on SCOP

title: Who Really Owns Your Heat Pump? Mapping the Parent Companies
author: Heat Pump Database
summary: 77 manufacturers in this database collapse into a much smaller set of corporate parents. We mapped which brands share an owner, including two ownership changes that only completed in the last two months.
image_credit: Heat Pump Database, brand ownership map showing 8 parent groups and 19 subsidiary brands
tldr: Eight corporate groups own 19 of the 77 heat pump brands in this database between them. The biggest recent moves: Carrier sold Riello to Ariston Group in July 2026, and Bosch absorbed Johnson Controls' York and Hitachi lines in January 2026.
body_html:
Scroll through the manufacturers list on this site and it reads like 77 independent companies. In practice, a chunk of that list collapses into a much smaller set of corporate parents, several of which have reshuffled their heat pump brands within the last 18 months. Below are the ownership links we could confirm from company announcements and filings, focused only on the parents and subsidiaries that are both represented in this database.

Two of these groups changed hands within the last two months of this article being published: Riello moved from Carrier to Ariston Group on 1 July 2026, and Bosch finished absorbing Johnson Controls’ York and Hitachi lines in January 2026. Ownership in this industry moves fast, so treat this as a snapshot rather than a permanent map.

Carrier Global Corporation

Carrier owns Carrier and CIAT outright, and completed its acquisition of Viessmann’s Climate Solutions business, the heat pump and boiler side of the company, in January 2024 for around €12 billion. Carrier also holds the rights to sell Toshiba-branded heat pumps across Europe under a separate licensing arrangement with Toshiba Corporation, which otherwise remains independent. Riello was part of this group until Carrier sold it to Ariston Group in July 2026.

Ariston Group

Ariston and Riello are now siblings: Ariston Group completed its purchase of Riello’s heating and heat pump business from Carrier on 1 July 2026, for gross proceeds of around $440 million.

Vaillant Group

Vaillant and Glow-worm sit under the same German family-owned group. Glow-worm is part of Vaillant’s “Saunier Duval Brand Group” alongside Saunier Duval and Protherm, neither of which are stocked in this database.

Groupe Atlantic

Atlantic, Ideal Heating and Clade are all Groupe Atlantic brands, alongside Gledhill, Hamworthy and Keston, which aren’t in this database. Groupe Atlantic itself was recently majority-acquired by Paloma Rheem Holdings.

NIBE Group

Nibe, CTC and Rhoss are all NIBE Industrier AB brands: CTC came with the 2016–17 acquisition of Enertech Group, and Rhoss became a wholly-owned NIBE subsidiary in January 2019 after NIBE bought out the remaining stake from the Bellò family.

Bosch Home Comfort Group

This is the newest and largest cluster here. Bosch completed its purchase of Johnson Controls’ residential and light-commercial HVAC business, including the Johnson Controls–Hitachi joint venture, with the integration finishing in January 2026. Bosch, York and Hitachi (for residential and light-commercial units) now share one parent.

Johnson Controls

Johnson Controls kept its industrial refrigeration and heat pump business when it sold the residential side to Bosch, so Sabroe remains a Johnson Controls brand, just a smaller one than before.

Midea Group

Midea holds an 80% stake in Clivet, acquired in 2016; the Bellò family that founded Clivet retained the remaining 20%.

What this means if you're comparing quotes

None of this means sibling brands are identical products with different badges; Carrier, CIAT and Viessmann heat pumps, for instance, are built to different specifications and sold through different channels. But it's worth knowing when two quotes you're comparing ultimately report to the same boardroom, particularly for warranty terms, parts availability and who you're actually negotiating with if you push back on price.
seo_title: Who Really Owns Your Heat Pump? Brand Parent Companies
meta_description: 77 heat pump brands in our database share a much smaller set of corporate parents. We mapped who owns whom, including two recent ownership changes.

title: Baxi Launches High-Output Auriga HP+ Heat Pumps up to 170 kW
author: Heat Pump Database
summary: Baxi has extended its R290 Auriga HP+ commercial air source heat pump range to 170 kW, with a standard model and a quieter ES version for noise-sensitive sites.
image_credit: Baxi Auriga HP+ 50-170 kW. Image: Baxi
tldr: Two new reversible R290 models: Auriga HP+ (50-170 kW, up to 70 °C) and the quieter Auriga HP+ ES (55-170 kW, about 8 dB(A) lower).
body_html:
Baxi has added two higher-output models to its commercial Auriga HP+ air source heat pump family. The new units take the range from small plant-room sizes up to 170 kW, and like the rest of the HP+ line they use natural R290 (propane) refrigerant. Baxi announced the launch on 28 September 2026.

Two versions

  • Auriga HP+ (50–170 kW) – the standard high-output model, aimed at buildings where comfort and control matter most. It can be ordered with factory-fitted options and produces hot water at up to 70 °C, so it can be dropped into existing systems that still run on radiators.
  • Auriga HP+ ES (55–170 kW) – the low-noise variant. EC inverter axial fans move the same air at lower speed, which Baxi says cuts sound levels by around 8 dB(A). That makes it the one to look at for noise-sensitive sites.

Heating, cooling and hot water from one unit

Both versions are reversible, so a single machine can provide space heating, cooling and domestic hot water. Baxi is positioning them for new build and retrofit projects across the UK and Ireland, naming education and healthcare estates, offices, hotels and energy centres as typical applications. Shane Suter, Baxi’s Commercial Business Director, described the expanded range as “a practical, flexible route to lower-carbon heating and cooling”.

The new 50–170 kW models sit above the existing Baxi Auriga HP (20–40 kW, R32) and Auriga HP+ 20–30 kW (R290) units. The 20 and 30 kW HP+ models are already in this database; we’ll add the larger sizes once Baxi publishes full technical data.

Source: Baxi UK, “Baxi launches high-output Auriga HP+ air source heat pump series” (28 September 2026).
seo_title: Baxi Launches High-Output Auriga HP+ Heat Pumps
meta_description: Baxi extends its R290 Auriga HP+ commercial air source heat pump range to 170 kW: a standard model with 70 °C hot water and a quieter ES version.

title: Viessmann Launches the Vitocal 200-A ie Heat Pump for UK Homes
image_credit: Viessmann Vitocal 200-A ie outdoor unit. Image: Viessmann
seo_title: Viessmann Vitocal 200-A ie: New R290 Heat Pump for UK Homes
summary: Viessmann has launched the Vitocal 200-A ie, a 4-12 kW R290 monobloc aimed at the price-conscious UK market, with one app to run heat pump, solar, battery and EV charger.
meta_description: Viessmann launches the Vitocal 200-A ie: a 4-12 kW R290 monobloc for UK homes with 75 °C flow, A+++ rating and smart control of solar, battery and EV charging.
tldr: A 4-12 kW R290 monobloc with 75 °C flow, A+++ efficiency and a new controller that links heat pump, solar PV, batteries and EV chargers in the ViCare app.
body_html:
Viessmann Climate Solutions launched the Vitocal 200-A ie (“intelligent energy”) at InstallerSHOW at the NEC on 23 June 2026. It is a monobloc air-to-water heat pump pitched squarely at the entry- to mid-level end of the UK market, which Viessmann describes as the fastest-growing segment, and it went on sale in the autumn.

Key specifications

  • Outputs from 4 to 12 kW, which Viessmann says covers roughly 70–80% of UK homes
  • Natural R290 refrigerant and an A+++ energy rating
  • Flow temperatures up to 75 °C, useful for retrofits with existing radiators and fast hot water recovery
  • Single-fan outdoor unit up to 12 kW, about 90 cm installed height, roughly 90–118 kg depending on size
  • Sound levels of 54 or 56 dB(A) in noise-reduced mode
  • Pump and electric heater moved into the outdoor unit; up to four units can be cascaded (48 kW) off one indoor unit

One controller for the whole home

The bigger story is the software. The Vitocal 200-A ie is the first product on Viessmann’s new One Base Intelligence platform. A wall- or cylinder-mounted Universal Controller ie (45 × 40 × 13.5 cm) links the heat pump with solar PV, battery storage, ventilation and EV chargers – including other brands – and presents everything in the ViCare app. It can automate time-of-use tariffs and receives over-the-air updates, and Viessmann says the controller can also be used on its own to bring third-party equipment into ViCare.

The unit was developed with input from UK installers, is made in the EU and has already picked up an iF Design Award.

The Vitocal 200-A ie is in this database: 6 kW, 8 kW, 10 kW and 12 kW models, with full specs and test conditions.

Source: Viessmann UK, “New Intelligent Heat Pump is Gateway to the Fully Electrified Home” (22 June 2026).

title: NIBE Launches the Next-Generation S2060 R290 Heat Pump
image_credit: NIBE S2060 models in the Heat Pump Database. Chart: Heat Pump Database
seo_title: NIBE S2060: Next-Generation R290 Heat Pump Launched
summary: NIBE has launched the S2060, the first of a new family of compact R290 heat pumps, with SCOP up to 5.33, 75 °C flow and no R290 protective zone needed.
meta_description: NIBE launches the S2060, its first next-generation compact R290 heat pump: SCOP up to 5.33, 75 °C flow, heating and cooling to -25 °C and no protective zone.
tldr: First of a new compact R290 family: SCOP up to 5.33, flow to 75 °C, heating and cooling down to -25 °C, single fan, and no R290 protective zone requirement.
body_html:
NIBE marked 20 years in the UK by unveiling the S2060, the first model in a new family of compact air source heat pumps using natural R290 refrigerant. More outputs are due to follow later in the year.

What’s new

  • SCOP of up to 5.33
  • Flow temperatures up to 75 °C
  • Heating and cooling down to −25 °C outside
  • No R290 protective zone requirement, giving more freedom when siting the unit
  • Compact single-fan casing, lighter and quieter than previous NIBE generations
  • Works with NIBE’s existing F- and S-series indoor controls and the myUplink app

Built around the installer

NIBE’s pitch is that the S2060 is easier to specify and fit, not just more efficient. Installers on the first two UK jobs highlighted the compact size and simple installation. Managing Director Paul Smith framed the launch as the start of a new product generation for NIBE in the UK, backed by continued investment in training and installer support.

Two S2060 models are in this database so far: S2060-6 (8.27 kW, SCOP 5.33, 51 dB(A)) and S2060-10 (11.73 kW, SCOP 5.07, 54 dB(A)). We’ll add further sizes as NIBE releases them.

Source: NIBE UK, “Built for what’s next: NIBE’s next-generation S2060” (July 2026).

title: Vaillant's Remastered aroTHERM plus Keeps Its Quiet Mark
image_credit: Vaillant aroTHERM plus models in the Heat Pump Database. Chart: Heat Pump Database
seo_title: Vaillant's Remastered aroTHERM plus Keeps Its Quiet Mark
summary: Six years after the original, Vaillant has launched a remastered aroTHERM plus. It keeps its Quiet Mark, and the new 7 kW model was named best for homes with limited space.
meta_description: Vaillant launches the remastered aroTHERM plus R290 heat pump: still Quiet Mark approved, with a new 7 kW model and a Flexible Space Function for tight sites.
tldr: A remastered aroTHERM plus launched in June 2026. It keeps Quiet Mark approval, and the 7 kW model adds a Flexible Space Function that allows much smaller clearances.
body_html:
Vaillant’s aroTHERM plus has been one of the UK’s most-installed heat pumps since it launched in 2020. In June 2026 Vaillant released a remastered aroTHERM plus, updating the design and features while keeping the R290 platform.

Still Quiet Mark approved

Noise is one of the most common worries for people considering a heat pump. The new aroTHERM plus carries the same Quiet Mark certification as the original. Vaillant says its heat pumps were the first ever to hold Quiet Mark, back in 2014.

New 7 kW model for tight spaces

The new 7 kW model introduces a Flexible Space Function, which allows much smaller clearances below windows and beside doors. That makes it easier to site on small plots and terraces. Quiet Mark’s Poppy Szkiler picked it as the best option for homes with limited space in a round-up of quiet heat pumps for The Times.

Vaillant also points homeowners to the Visit a Heat Pump scheme, which lets people see a working installation and talk to the owner before committing.

See the Vaillant range in this database, including the aroTHERM plus 7 kW and other sizes, with COP, flow temperature and sound power for each.

Source: Vaillant UK, “The aroTHERM plus heat pump, can the good really get better?” (2026).

title: Stiebel Eltron Marks 50 Years of Heat Pumps With Wider hpnext Range
image_credit: Stiebel Eltron HPA-O 2026 models in the Heat Pump Database. Chart: Heat Pump Database
seo_title: Stiebel Eltron Expands hpnext Heat Pump Range for 2026
summary: For its 50th year making heat pumps, Stiebel Eltron UK has added new sizes to the HPA-O Trend HC and Plus HC air source ranges, plus white Plus units and new packs.
meta_description: Stiebel Eltron expands its hpnext HPA-O Trend HC and Plus HC air source ranges for 2026 with new 5-17 kW sizes, white Plus units and pre-configured packs.
tldr: New 5, 7 and 13 kW 230 V Trend HC units and 10 kW Plus HC models; Plus range in white or anthracite; new SBB 200 Trend cylinder and pre-configured packs.
body_html:
Stiebel Eltron UK is celebrating 50 years of heat pump manufacturing by widening its hpnext air source line-up, launched the year before. The HPA-O 13.2 Trend HC 230 replaces the older WPL-A 25 ACS models.

The 2026 line-up

  • HPA-O Trend HC (anthracite): 230 V models at 4.91, 6.92, 9.49 and 12.47 kW, and 400 V models at 9.49 and 17.36 kW. The 5, 7 and 13 kW 230 V units are new.
  • HPA-O Plus HC (anthracite or white): 230 V at 7.09 and 10.07 kW, 400 V at 10.07 and 13.15 kW. The 10 kW models are new, and all four Plus units will be offered in white later in the year.

Stiebel Eltron has also added the lightweight SBB 200 Trend hot water cylinder and re-configured heat pump packs that bundle compatible components. The company says the hpnext models are the quietest heat pumps it has made.

All of these models are in this database, for example the HPA-O 05.2 Trend HC and HPA-O 07.2 Plus HC (SCOP 5.09, 43 dB(A)). Browse the full Stiebel Eltron range.

Source: Stiebel Eltron UK, “STIEBEL ELTRON celebrates 50 years of heat pumps with expanded portfolio” (2026).

title: Ferroli Adds 26-35 kW Models to the OMNIA LIFE M R290 Range
image_credit: Ferroli OMNIA LIFE M 26T-35T in the Heat Pump Database. Chart: Heat Pump Database
seo_title: Ferroli OMNIA LIFE M R290 Adds 26T, 30T and 35T Models
summary: Ferroli has extended its OMNIA LIFE M R290 monobloc range with high-output 26T, 30T and 35T models for larger homes and light commercial buildings.
meta_description: Ferroli extends the OMNIA LIFE M R290 monobloc range with 26, 30 and 35 kW three-phase models: water up to 80 °C, A+++ at 35 °C and cascades of up to six units.
tldr: New 26, 30 and 35 kW three-phase R290 monoblocs: inverter compressor, water up to 80 °C, A+++/A++, built-in hydronics and cascades of up to six units.
body_html:
Ferroli has added three high-output models – 26T, 30T and 35T – to its OMNIA LIFE M range of R290 air-to-water heat pumps, taking the monobloc family into medium-sized residential and commercial projects.

Key features

  • Natural R290 refrigerant and a DC inverter compressor that modulates output
  • Supplied as complete outdoor units with an integrated hydronic kit
  • Heating and cooling, rated A+++ at 35 °C and A++ at 55 °C
  • Water temperatures up to 80 °C, suitable for radiators, underfloor heating, fan coils and hot water via an external cylinder
  • Cascade one master with up to five slave units for larger buildings
  • Remote monitoring through Ferroli’s MYOMNIA SMART app

Ferroli designs the range in Italy and presents it as part of its wider push into low-carbon HVAC.

All three models are in this database: OMNIA LIFE M 26T (SCOP 4.95), 30T (SCOP 4.93) and 35T (SCOP 4.48).

Source: Ferroli, “The OMNIA LIFE M R290 range expands with new high-capacity models 26T–35T” (5 May 2026).

title: Carrier Launches AquaForce 61XWHVZE High-Temperature Heat Pump
summary: Carrier has launched the AquaForce 61XWHVZE, a packaged high-temperature water-source heat pump for district heating and industry that can run on waste heat, ground water or geothermal sources.
meta_description: Carrier launches the AquaForce 61XWHVZE, a packaged high-temperature water-source heat pump for district heating and industry using ultra-low-GWP HFOs.
tldr: A ready-to-install, variable-speed water-source heat pump for high-temperature district and industrial heating, using ultra-low-GWP refrigerants and Eurovent-certified performance.
body_html:
Carrier announced the AquaForce 61XWHVZE from its Montluel site in France on 24 March 2026. It is a packaged, high-temperature water-source heat pump aimed at district heating networks and industrial process heat – markets where electrifying heat is becoming central to decarbonisation plans.

What it is

  • A factory-built, ready-to-use package designed to shorten project timelines
  • Variable-speed compressor with Carrier’s GreenSpeed Intelligence, tuned for seasonal efficiency without losing full-load output
  • Ultra-low-GWP refrigerant options (HFO R-1234ze or R-515B), with no on-site combustion emissions
  • Works from almost any water-based heat source: grey water, data-centre waste heat, deep ground water and geothermal
  • Compact footprint, and can be supplied containerised as a complete system
  • Eurovent-certified performance and integration with Carrier’s PlantCTRL plant controls for pumps, valves and auxiliaries

Why it matters

Carrier positions the 61XWHVZE as a way for heat networks and industrial users to cut fossil fuel use as energy prices rise, and to recover heat that is currently wasted. Hybrid set-ups with Carrier group boilers and heating products are also supported.

The 61XWHVZE is not yet in this database. Its sister water-source ranges are: see the AquaForce 61XWHLZE and 61XWH-ZE, or the full Carrier range. We’ll add the 61XWHVZE once full technical data is published.

Source: Carrier Europe, “High-Temperature Heating for district heating and industrial application” (24 March 2026).

title: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Adds 10 kW and 14 kW Hydrolution EZY R290 Models
image_credit: Hydrolution EZY R290 models in the Heat Pump Database. Chart: Heat Pump Database
seo_title: MHI Hydrolution EZY R290 Adds 10 kW and 14 kW Models
summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Air-Conditioning Europe has added 10 kW and 14 kW models to its Hydrolution EZY R290 monobloc range, for larger homes and small commercial sites.
meta_description: MHIAE adds 10 kW and 14 kW models to the Hydrolution EZY R290 monobloc heat pump range: 75 °C flow, -25 to +43 °C operation and a quiet mode down to 57 dB(A).
tldr: New 10 and 14 kW R290 monoblocs from June 2026: flow to 75 °C, -25 to +43 °C operation, built-in leak detection and a silent mode down to 57 dB(A).
body_html:
Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Air-Conditioning Europe (MHIAE) has extended its Hydrolution EZY R290 monobloc air-to-water heat pump range with new 10 kW and 14 kW models, available from June 2026. They take the range, which started with 6.0 and 7.1 kW units, into larger homes and small commercial buildings.

Key features

  • Natural R290 refrigerant, fully sealed in the outdoor unit – only two water pipes and a power cable to connect
  • Flow temperatures up to 75 °C, operating from −25 °C to +43 °C outside without a backup heater
  • Heating, cooling and domestic hot water
  • Built-in refrigerant leak sensor that shuts the unit down and runs the fan to disperse any leak
  • Dual vibration isolation, triple-layer sound insulation and a large fan; the 14 kW model is rated at 63 dB(A) sound power, dropping to 57 dB(A) in silent mode
  • All-black casing with a silver accent that hides the fan from the side

The 6.0 and 7.1 kW models already hold MCS and Heat Pump Keymark approval, and MHIAE says accreditation is planned for the new sizes. As with all MHIAE products, they are sold only through its European distributor network.

All Hydrolution EZY R290 sizes are in this database: 6.0 kW, 7.1 kW, 10 kW and 14 kW, with single- and three-phase versions of the larger units.

Source: MHIAE, “MHIAE Launches higher capacity Hydrolution EZY R290 Heat Pump Models” (13 May 2026).
